episodes.title: I Left a 10,000-Person Cult Because of a Stranger’s Kindness
episodes.description:
A child raised in the FLDS cult learns early that kindness from outsiders can be more powerful than fear, and that lesson changes everything. Shane Jessop tells the story of growing up in the Utah-Arizona border community known as Short Creek, the pressure of being taught not to question, and the moment he finally walked away at 23.Born into a world of control, secrecy, and severe consequences for doubt, Shane describes what it was like to grow up as the second oldest of 22 kids, working heavy equipment from an early age while living under the constant warning that asking the wrong question could cost you your family. He shares how simple encounters with “outsiders” cracked open a different view of people, truth, and himself.

You’ll discover:

What life inside the FLDS looked like day to day, from no TV and no internet to the fear of questioning leadership
How Shane’s work with his dad’s excavating company gave him rare exposure to the outside world
Why a stranger helping a child at a gas station became a defining memory
The painful tension of being told you’re “bad” while your own conscience says otherwise
The chain of events that led to his final break from the community on April 6, 2011

Shane also shares the unforgettable story of Dorothy, a ranch owner whose unexpected kindness, honesty, and wisdom became a turning point at exactly the right time. What begins as a work trip in Nevada turns into a profound human connection, a tragedy, and the final nudge that confirms Shane can no longer stay where he is.This conversation is about more than escaping a cult. It’s about the power of integrity, the cost of control, and how one act of kindness can alter the course of a life. If you’re drawn to stories of resilience, faith, freedom, and the quiet moments that change everything, this episode will stay with you.Perfect for anyone who cares about overcoming adversity, cult recovery, faith deconstruction, or the surprising ways compassion can set people free.

Guest Credibility:


Shane Jessop is an entrepreneur and storyteller from Nashville, known for sharing his powerful firsthand experience growing up in and leaving the FLDS community. He is also working on a book that expands on the experiences he shares in this episode.
